solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Admit car design is striking

indicators.note: to design is to plan or lay out afresh, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that a car's styling makes it eye-catching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' looks like a noun about the car's looks, but it is the anagram signal on ADMIT and CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking makes a vivid impression, as a theatrical, showy effect does.

clue.text: Churchman's entertaining first-rate company in study

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: entertaining in the sense of hosting a guest, so the den takes the other letters in

parts.note: a den is a study or private room
A, as in A1, means first-rate

explanation.surface: A clergyman hosts a top-class firm in his study.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained minister ranking below a priest, so a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Very impressed when rower picked up fast, catching race leader

indicators.note: picked up as in heard, so the word for rower is spelt as it sounds in non-rhotic speech

parts.note: an oar is a rower, one who pulls an oar in a crew

indicators.note: catching says the word for fast holds the leading letter

parts.note: stuck fast means firmly fixed

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of race

explanation.surface: A rower was quickly hauled aboard after grabbing the leader in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like being hauled out of the water, but it signals a homophone of OAR. 'fast' is fixed firm, not speedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone struck with awe is overwhelmed with wonder and admiration.

clue.text: Not allowed to win when hosting race, chap keeps order

indicators.note: hosting says the word for when takes the word for win inside it

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as he left'
to gain is to win
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
a chap is a he
a ruler keeps order, so rules does the same job

explanation.surface: A man running a race keeps order so that nobody is allowed to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prohibited by regulations is forbidden, not permitted.

clue.text: Is concealing politician's unpaid bill disrespectful?

indicators.note: concealing says the word is hides the other letters inside it

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: A question about whether hiding an MP's unpaid debt is rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking reverence for God or religion, so irreverent, showing no proper respect.

clue.text: Lick ends of hair in moustache

indicators.note: in says the picked letters sit inside the slang word for moustache

parts.note: tash is informal British slang for a moustache

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters, here taken from hair

explanation.surface: Someone licks the tips of the hairs in their moustache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lick' reads as using the tongue, but in sport to lick a rival is to beat them soundly.
explanation.definitionFit: To lick an opponent is to defeat them heavily, a synonym for beating them.

clue.text: Chinese dynasty legends later become a children's story

parts.note: the Han dynasty ruled China from about 206 BC to AD 220

indicators.note: become says these letters turn into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Old Chinese myths turned later into a tale for kids.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brothers Grimm fairy tale about two siblings lost in the woods and a witch's gingerbread house.

clue.text: Stone's mounted in bracelet again

indicators.note: mounted says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters are found inside the words bracelet again

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gem is set in the bracelet once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Draft lacked the indicator 'in' on the hidden step; added. 'mounted' looks like a jeweller's setting, but in a down clue it means read upwards; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded variety of chalcedony, a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: Henry has paper on Queen Mary to start in school holiday

parts.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
FT is the Financial Times newspaper
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: to start picks the first letter of the name Mary

explanation.surface: Henry has a newspaper story about Queen Mary to begin the school break.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the newspaper this puzzle appears in.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools, a short break of about a week in the middle of each term.

clue.text: Still in charge after short panic

indicators.note: after puts the in-charge abbreviation behind the shortened word
short says the last letter of the word for panic is cut off

parts.note: being in a state is being in a panic

explanation.surface: Someone in command, after a brief panic, stays calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means not moving or changing, motionless.

clue.text: A large cutback in online help

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes
split into two words: axe, meaning chop, then back, so axe in reverse order

explanation.surface: A big reduction in the support offered online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutback' reads as one word meaning a reduction; split it into 'cut' (axe) and 'back', telling you to write it the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazon's voice assistant answers questions and controls devices through the internet.

clue.text: Trouble after Russian leader has judge locked up

indicators.note: after puts the word for trouble behind the leader and the judge

parts.note: Vladimir Putin is the Russian president
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A judge causes problems by sending the Russian president to prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone imprisoned has been locked up in a cell.

clue.text: Perfect old-fashioned party held by eccentric aunt

parts.note: styles that are out are no longer fashionable

indicators.note: held by says the party word sits inside the jumbled aunt
eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of aunt are rearranged

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: An oddball aunt throws a quaint, dated party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfect' here is the intensifying sense, as in 'a perfect stranger'; 'eccentric' rearranges AUNT to ANUT, which holds DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean complete or utter, as in a thorough rogue: an intensifier before a noun.

clue.text: Put up net centrally on court

indicators.note: centrally picks the middle letter of the word net

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Someone sets up the net in the middle of a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect a structure is to build or put it up, as with a tent or fence.

clue.text: Question as to allocation of shares

indicators.note: an allocation shares things out, so the letters of as to are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: A query about how shares in a company are to be allotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allocation of shares' reads as one financial phrase; 'allocation of' is the anagram signal on AS TO, and 'shares' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Quotas are fixed portions allotted to each party, that is, set shares of a total.

clue.text: Cleaning lady receives award from Queen in private room

indicators.note: receives says the honour goes inside the word for cleaning lady

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British cleaning lady
the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is an honour conferred by the monarch

explanation.surface: A cleaner is honoured by the Queen in a private audience.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British cleaning woman, paid by the hour; the MBE is a royal honour often given to long-serving workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is an old word for a bedroom or private apartment in a house.

clue.text: Earthmover vehicle removing last sleeper on lines

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the word for sleeper below, after, the lines abbreviation
removing last says the final letter of the vehicle is dropped

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural
a dozer is someone who dozes, a sleeper

explanation.surface: A digger travels with no sleeper at the end of the railway lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleeper' and 'lines' suggest a railway, but they are DOZER and LL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracked tractor with a broad blade for shifting soil, an earthmoving machine.

clue.text: Dad raised a child without expert method

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go around the expert
raised in a down clue says the word for dad is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: pa is a word for dad
a pro is an expert

explanation.surface: A father brought up a child without any expert help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has its old sense 'outside', as in the hymn's 'a green hill far away, without a city wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: An approach is a way of dealing with something, a manner or technique.

clue.text: Served a chop with sides of kohlrabi and cabbage

indicators.note: served as in dished up in a fresh arrangement, so these letters are rearranged
the sides of a word are its first and last letters, taken from kohlrabi

explanation.surface: A chop was served with side dishes of kohlrabi and cabbage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides of kohlrabi' gives K and I, which join A CHOP in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: This leafy Chinese vegetable is a variety of cabbage, often stir-fried.

clue.text: Spent too much time following trendy society girl

indicators.note: following puts the time abbreviation after the other pieces

parts.note: something in is fashionable
a deb, or debutante, is a young woman entering high society

explanation.surface: A fashionable socialite blew too much money.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has overspent owes money, being in the red with creditors.

clue.text: Whiskey and beer-drinking daughters walk unsteadily

parts.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: drinking says the beer word takes the daughters inside it

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
D is the abbreviation for daughter, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Daughters who have been on the whisky and beer stagger about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beer-drinking' looks like a description of the daughters, but it is the beer that does the drinking, swallowing the daughters.
explanation.definitionFit: To waddle is to walk with short swaying steps, like a duck, so the gait is unsteady.

clue.text: Want to live north of Cambridge in Fen town

indicators.note: in says the pieces go inside the word for want

parts.note: a wish is a want
to be is to exist or live

indicators.note: north of in a down clue means the top of the word Cambridge, its first letter

explanation.surface: Wanting to live north of Cambridge, in a town in the Fens.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are the flat drained marshland of eastern England; the surface is geographically accurate, since this town lies north of Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: This market town lies in the Fens of north Cambridgeshire.

clue.text: Keep working and delay leaving

parts.note: to keep healthy is to stay healthy, so keep means stay
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Someone carries on with the job and puts off going.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a double definition, and works as one, but the blog's charade uses every word.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain somewhere longer rather than going is to linger, putting off departure.

clue.text: Jockey has clear run after final hurdle

indicators.note: after puts the run abbreviation behind the last letter of hurdle

parts.note: to rid a place of something is to clear it

indicators.note: final picks the last letter of the word hurdle

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A jockey is well clear after the last fence in a hurdles race.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockey rides racehorses, so is a horse rider by profession.

clue.text: Sewer's covering centre of rip with complicated darn

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: covering says the jumbled letters go around the middle letter
complicated means twisted or tangled, so the letters of darn are mixed up
centre of picks the middle letter of the word rip

explanation.surface: A seamstress covers a tear with a tricky darn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' reads as someone who sews, but it is a waste pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A drain is a pipe carrying off waste water, as a sewer does.

clue.text: Cast doubt on policeman's commendation

parts.note: a DI is a detective inspector, so a policeman's is DI'S
credit is praise or acknowledgement, a commendation

explanation.surface: Suspicion is thrown on an officer's award for good work.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit a claim is to make people doubt it or harm its reputation.

clue.text: Top grade face covering reportedly fitted for free

parts.note: A is the top grade in exams

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for face covering is taken as it sounds, spelt another way

parts.note: a veil covers a face
fitted for a task means able to do it

explanation.surface: A first-rate face mask that has been fitted is handed out at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: VEIL is said aloud and written VAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone free at a time is not busy, so can be met or called on then.

clue.text: Pointless little sleep feeding state of anxiety

indicators.note: feeding says the sleep symbol goes into the shortened word
pointless says a compass point, here the letter N, is taken away from the word for little

parts.note: tiny means little
ZZ is the cartoon symbol for sleep or snoring

explanation.surface: Fretting over a pointless short nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' looks like 'futile', but it removes N, a compass point, from TINY, leaving TIY to take in ZZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A tizzy is an informal word for a nervous, flustered state of agitation.

clue.text: Entrench one's troops, holding up front

indicators.note: holding says the letters are held within the run of words entrench one's troops

explanation.surface: An order to dig in and keep the forces holding the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up front' reads as the military front line, but it means candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone up front is frank and open, telling the plain truth.

clue.text: Young adults mostly relax around geek

definitions.note: read as the young of adults, that is, the offspring of grown-ups

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of the word for relax is dropped

parts.note: to chill is to relax

indicators.note: around says the word for geek is turned round

parts.note: a nerd is a geek

explanation.surface: Young grown-ups mostly chill out around some techie type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young adults' looks like teenagers, but it means adults' young, their offspring. 'mostly' drops the last letter of the word for relax; 'around' turns the geek word round.
explanation.definitionFit: The offspring of grown-ups are their kids, the young of the species.
